routes.description: Establish that consciousness or mind is fundamental by presenting idealism as the more economical explanation of experience, information, causation, and observer-linked quantum phenomena, while supplying an account of physical development and an empirical condition that could undermine the view.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if its ontology explains experienced and physical regularities without an indispensable material substrate, connects quantum observation to consciousness without preventing pre-observer development, and identifies a publicly examinable way in which the account could fail.

motionBridge.description: Show that idealism and the cited quantum considerations jointly provide good reason to treat consciousness or a divine mind as fundamental.

centralBridges.description: Establish a cumulative inference from mental correlations, top-down causation, informational structure, and limits of material reduction to an idealist ontology.
Explain how informational evolution and observer-linked definite appearances can accommodate physical interaction and cosmic development before local conscious observers.
State empirical implications or potential defeaters that make the consciousness-dependent account publicly examinable rather than insulated from evidence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Support the ontology by arguing that experienced properties and informational distinctions do not require an additional material substance.
Clarify what interactions and structures remain as informational evolution when no thinking observer produces definite spatiotemporal appearances.

routes.description: Require independently confirmable manifestations and mind-independent causal interaction for the affirmative claim, distinguish legitimate inference from unsupported ontology, and test whether consciousness-dependent physics explains preconscious development or instead adds an unfalsifiable divine or mental condition.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the proposed idealist and quantum inferences lack independently demonstrable support, fail to account for physical interaction and development without observer dependence, or do not yield discriminating empirical consequences sufficient to justify fundamentality.

motionBridge.description: Show that the claim of fundamental consciousness or divine mind fails the relevant public-demonstrability or physical-interaction requirements.

centralBridges.description: Establish that burden-bearing claims require detectable, repeatable, and independently confirmable consequences in shared reality.
Distinguish inferences built from mutually reinforcing demonstrable evidence from an idealist inference whose components may not independently support its ontology.
Account for forces, chemistry, and physical development through causal relations that do not depend on being mentally experienced.
Determine whether observer-dependent reality has a discriminating falsification condition and whether its additional mental commitments perform necessary explanatory work.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test the account against evolution and chemical interaction occurring before ordinary conscious observers were present.
Examine whether informational and video-game analogies entail the claimed absence of definite or maintained unobserved physical structure.

sections.title: Public Evidence and Explanatory Inference
sections.rationale: This issue sets the governing evidential burden and tests whether the affirmative cumulative inference resembles established evidence-based inference closely enough to support a fundamental ontology.

sections.title: Information, Experience, and Material Substrate
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether experienced properties, mathematics, and informational distinctions make matter explanatorily redundant or whether physical properties denote mind-independent causal capacities.

sections.title: Observer Dependence and Preconscious Development
sections.rationale: This issue is central to whether an observer-linked quantum account can accommodate evolution, chemistry, and continuing interaction before local minds without relying on an unexplained divine observer.

sections.title: Unobserved Reality and Physical Interaction
sections.rationale: This issue tests what persists without thinking minds and whether analogies involving rendering or informational evolution support the claimed relation between observation, spacetime definiteness, and causal interaction.

sections.title: Falsifiability and Ontological Parsimony
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether the consciousness-dependent account exposes itself to a discriminating empirical defeater and whether its ontological commitments satisfy the debate's demonstrability and economy requirements.
